method: For each of b1.7.3, b1.8.1, 1.0, 1.2.5 and 1.8.9 the entry was located in https://piston-meta.mojang.com/mc/game/version_manifest_v2.json, its per-version metadata JSON was fetched, and downloads.client was downloaded to %TEMP%\mce-boundaries\artifacts\<version>-client.jar. SHA-1 and byte size were asserted against the metadata before any use; all five matched. Registry classes were identified without relying on obfuscated names: every .class entry of each jar was read as raw bytes and searched with the case-sensitive word-boundary regex (?<![A-Za-z])NAME(?![A-Za-z]) for a probe set of known mob names and known item names. In every version one class matched a large majority of the probes and the runner-up matched only about three, so the identification is unambiguous: entities jc/um/afw/aao/pm and items gm/sv/acy/yr/zw for b1.7.3/b1.8.1/1.0/1.2.5/1.8.9. Each identified class's constant pool was then parsed in full: CONSTANT_Utf8 entries and the CONSTANT_String entries that reference them were enumerated exhaustively, and <clinit> was disassembled with real bytecode offsets. Entity names are the String operand of each register call a(Class,String,int); item names are the registry class's full CONSTANT_String set minus an explicit exclusion list of non-name literals. All matching was case-sensitive and carried out on raw bytes, so gm.J and gm.j remain distinct. Mechanics that are not registry entries were resolved behaviourally: the relevant class was disassembled with javap (JDK 25.0.4.1) and, where needed, by direct bytecode-offset inspection, citing method names and code offsets. No Minecraft code, decompiled source or asset was copied; only identifiers, hashes and behavioural facts are recorded.

versions.itemNamesSource: all printable CONSTANT_Utf8 entries referenced by CONSTANT_String in the identified item registry class, minus an explicit exclusion list of non-name literals (nonIdent excluded: ['.name', '13', 'CONFLICT @ ', 'Max stack size must be 1 for items with crafting results', 'item.'])

Item rows whose name is derived from a Block are not present as String literals in the item registry class (e.g. the crafting-table item name is block-derived).

mechanics.evidence: whole-jar exhaustive byte scan of b1.7.3-client.jar (sha1 43db9b498cb67058d2e12d394e6507722e71bb45) found no "sprint" substring anywhere in any class file, no sprint attribute-modifier UUID "662A6B8D-DA3E-4C1C-8813-96EA6097278D", no "Sprinting speed boost" literal, and no "key.sprint" keybinding; keybinding class kv declares exactly 10 key.* bindings and none is sprint

1.8.9 item names are reported as the complete CONSTANT_String set of the item registry class zw (356 identifiers after excluding '.name', 'item.', '+4', '11', '13', one UUID, and the block-state subtype tokens 'default', 'chiseled', 'lines'). 187 registration call sites yield 174 distinct names, so the String set is a superset; 185 String entries were not observed at a 3-arg registration call and are believed to be legacy-name aliases and block-derived item names. Individual membership of those 185 was not proven entry-by-entry.

Block-derived item names (for example the crafting-table item) are not String literals in the item registry class at any version; the effective item name space is the union of the item registry's own names and the names inherited from the block registry. This union was not enumerated item-by-item.
